rules.one_arm_at_a_time: one training arm uses the fleet at a time; the recorded control curve (runs ac/kc/o4, flat at 51% vs Ham) is the baseline, no control arm
rules.checkpoints: 25k games: kill only if the learner is unhealthy. 50k: kill if panel flat AND the card's leading indicator flat AND Ham <= control. 100k: kill if Ham < control - 0.5 or panel flat; else run to 300k. 300k: promote (Pig match, ablation) if >= control + 1.5.
rules.yardsticks: Ham: 10k network-only games on random boards (±0.5; control band 50.0-51.7). Panel: win rate vs held-out board specialists on their boards (4 boards now, ±0.4 mean; 100 boards from sp3 soon). Surprise: KL(search target || prior) in the learner log (0.06 = plateau). Fork gaps: main-line minus forked-alternative result.

cards.title: Self-play engine throughput (agent-driven profiling and optimisation)
cards.hypothesis: Games per core-second is what buys experiments: a 256-game shard takes 16 s (34 s for weak nets) on a 64-core actor. Known profile: Layer::forward 55%, encode+evaluate 11%, input compaction 8%, tree 5%. Targets: incremental observation encoding, allocation-free node expansion, cheaper chance-node copies.
cards.indicator: benchmark games/s and sims/s at 400/50 sims, 4 threads, same seed; all cargo tests green; numerics bit-identical or shown neutral by self-play
cards.kill: stop when remaining ideas are < 3% each
cards.notes: Working tree changes only (no commit, no maturin develop, no image push) while training jobs run; adopt via rebuild + push between arms.

cards.title: Separate opening network (initial placements only), evaluated on the board panel
cards.hypothesis: The missing Elo is one board-conditioned decision (the first placement). A dedicated network used only for the 8 placement decisions can be large (8x1024 or a GNN) at no play-time cost and trained on placement positions alone with sibling-averaged outcome targets and 2,400-sim policies; the main 4x512 net keeps the rest. Pig uses two opening-only evaluators the same way. Both the fine-tuned specialist and the from-scratch oracle converge on node 19 on board 1010194, so the target is learnable from outcomes; the open question is generalisation to held-out boards (hp1 memorised a 50-board pool).
cards.indicator: panel mean with the opening net swapped in (held-out boards), first-placement agreement with panel specialists; held-out opening value loss
cards.cost: ~1 day of engine + learner plumbing (two-net evaluator keyed on is_initial_build_phase, key option, bindings, Mirror, actor image; an opening learner reading shard opening positions and publishing models/opening_<run>.ctnn); then one arm (2 actors, ~2 h per 125k games)

cards.title: From-scratch single-board oracle (board 1010194)
cards.hypothesis: Board-specific strength comes from outcomes alone: a 4x512 net trained from random weights on one board reaches the fine-tuned specialist's level, uncontaminated by o3's habits, and beats Pig on that board.
cards.indicator: ladder on board 1010194 every 10 iterations (runs/fs1b.vs_o3): vs Camon, Spook, Breeze, o3-187, specialist (2k games each, ±1.1); vs random in the learner log
cards.kill: none (an oracle); stop when the curve is flat for ~30 iterations or at 02:00
cards.extend: if it passes the specialist: Pig match on the board (80 games) and re-run the opening/value mining against it as the teacher
cards.notes: fs1 (lr 3e-4, 6 shards/iter, reuse 4) diverged at iteration ~25 from random init: policy loss 44, value loss 93. Relaunched 21:30 as fs1b: lr 1e-4, reuse 2, 3 shards/iter. | 21:50: beats random 100% from 7k games; at 15k games policy loss 0.86 vs oh1's 0.96 at the same game count (same pace despite lr 1e-4), value loss higher (0.45 vs 0.24). Still ~0% vs Camon at 19k games; Camon itself was 30k games of training.
cards.result: 45k games from random weights on board 1010194: first placement converges to node 19 with prior 0.999 (the fine-tuned specialist's pick; o3-187 takes node 13), confirming the board knowledge is learnable from outcomes and that o3's pick is wrong here. But its general play is degenerate: 99.5% vs random, 0% vs Camon/Spook/Breeze/o3 from any openings (even Breeze's), 1,250-1,450 decisions per self-play game vs ~850: single-board self-play converges to a mirrored uncontested style. Not usable as a mid-game teacher or Pig test; the 20-iteration fine-tunes are strong because they inherit o3's play.

cards.hypothesis: The specialists' edge is ~8 pts of objectively better placements plus line-specific follow-up. Training the generalist's value head and opening policy on labels from hundreds of cheap specialists (on seeds disjoint from the panel) transfers the placement judgement across boards.

cards.title: Where the headroom is: specialists, opening swap, feature mining
cards.result: Specialists beat every o3 sibling 75-77% on their board (not exploitation); the 1010194 specialist beats Pig 73% where Ham gets 38.8% (first seat 15%); Ham's first pick there is the ore/wheat node 13 in 100% of games, the specialist's the brick/sheep/wheat node 19. Opening swap: placements are worth ~+8 pts under identical play; the specialist collapses from foreign openings (26.8%), so ~20 pts of its edge is line-specific follow-up. Search on placements (20k sims) recovers nothing. Mining: reach/contention beyond 2 roads explains 17% of mid-game value gap; first placement agreement with specialists 50%, per-resource valuation flips by board (except ore: specialists weight it less everywhere).

cards.title: on2: opening network + spot-structure input block (scarcity shares, resource pairs, numbers), continued from on1's weights
cards.hypothesis: Across the 100 board specialists, a linear ranking over hand features predicts the expert's first pick on 52% of held-out boards; scarcity (a spot's share of the board's supply of each resource) is the strongest group (-9 pts top-1 when removed), production and resource pairs next. The experts also prefer brick/wood over ore relative to o3-187. The opening net has to reconstruct these from raw tiles; given directly (board-constant, 5 + 54x13 + 1 inputs, zero-initialised so play is unchanged at start) it should learn board-specific first picks faster. Search cannot supply the signal: on 1010194 the 2,400-sim target puts 98.6% on node 13 vs the 89.5% prior, and 200k sims reaches 99.9%.

cards.title: Placement root-prior flattening over the plausible spots (search-side)
cards.hypothesis: Search amplifies the opening net's prior at placement roots (2,400 sims: 98.6% on the prior's pick), so flattening the root prior over the spots within 2 pips of the best would let the visit target move toward spots the prior underrates.
cards.indicator: 2,400-sim first-pick agreement with the 100 experts, flattened vs plain, before any training
cards.result: null-to-negative, killed before launch (13:00): on2@710 plain search agrees with the expert on 74/100, flattened (lambda 1, margin 2) on 69/100; on 1010194 the flattened search still puts 96.5% on node 13. The search's own values prefer the prior's pick: the error is in the value estimates, not the prior. Kept as MctsConfig::placement_flatten / --placement-flatten (default off).

cards.title: Forced-play first-pick win rates as a value target for the opening net
cards.hypothesis: The opening net's value head ranks first picks at Spearman 0.65 against forced win rates (experts 0.80) because single-game outcome labels are too noisy; clean win-rate labels would teach the ranking.
cards.indicator: runs/value_fit_test.py: fit on2's opening net to the 809 forced first-pick win rates of the 100 expert boards, 5-fold by board, held-out Spearman
cards.result: killed before launch (13:00): held-out Spearman 0.635 untouched -> 0.629 full fine-tune (train 0.99) / 0.577 head-only (train 0.71). Clean labels on 80 boards do not transfer to new boards and a linear probe on the trunk cannot even fit them in-sample: the inputs lack what the ranking needs. (Forks already give balanced one-game labels; averaging them adds no information per game.) -> on3 features.

cards.title: Opening board-count curve: first-pick learner with a fixed play policy over 1k / 10k / 100k boards (LoCM draft framing + Procgen level curve)
cards.hypothesis: The opening problem is zero-shot generalisation across boards (Procgen: hundreds of levels overfit, ~10k close the gap). With the play policy fixed (on2 nets, network-only) the first pick's value per board is cheap to label (8 pips-best picks x 48 games = 90 CPU-s per board, +-7 pts per label, two labelings agree on the best pick 68% of the time). Supervised fits on 130 and 1,000 boards both memorise (train 94-99% top-1) and get WORSE held out (48% -> 38%, experts 65 -> 53). If held-out agreement rises with 10k and 100k boards we are data-limited and an oracle actor mode is worth building; if it stays flat the inputs/architecture limit it and the per-spot network is next.
cards.indicator: runs/oracle_fit.py held-out pilot top-1 vs the oracle's best pick (ceiling ~68% at 48 games), expert agreement on the 100 specialist boards (65 untouched), value Spearman (0.63); learning curve in N boards

Held-out pilot top-1 vs the oracle's best pick, untouched -> best epoch -> last: 130 boards 59%->?; 1,022 boards 48% -> 48% -> 38%; 10,000 boards 47% -> 47% -> 42%, while the training boards reach 94-99% and expert agreement falls 65 -> 45-53 in every run. Ten times the boards gave no held-out gain at all. Label-noise ceiling 68% (two labelings agree on the best pick 27/40). The 100k point is not worth running. Next: spot-net (architecture), tested supervised on these 11k labelled boards first.

cards.title: Oracle actor mode: actors label plausible first picks (and later replies) on random boards with network-only playouts and ship the rows with the shards
cards.hypothesis: If open-curve shows held-out agreement rising with board count, the opening net needs balanced, low-noise labels over far more boards than self-play provides: a network-only playout costs ~1/25 of a search game, so an actor can label ~40 boards/h/core.

cards.title: Per-spot shared-weight opening head (hex-graph convolution / per-node MLP + pooling) instead of a flat MLP over 54 node blocks
cards.hypothesis: A flat MLP must learn the same 'is this spot good here' function 54 times with only the 12 symmetries to tie them together; the Catan placement thesis (TU Crete 2024) and Procgen both lean on convolutional inductive bias over the grid. If open-curve is flat in N, the representation is the limit and this is the lever.

cards.title: Micro-Catan: from-scratch self-play on the Mini map (24 land nodes) over N boards, the end-to-end RL version of the board-count curve
cards.hypothesis: Supervised fits with a fixed play policy cannot show whether self-play itself discovers openings given enough distinct boards. The Mini map makes games ~4x cheaper; training one base policy there and then opening-only learners over 100 / 1k / 10k / unlimited boards gives the RL curve.

cards.title: Placement targets from short-horizon playouts: K network-only playouts per plausible spot to turn T, averaged main-net value as the policy and value target (replaces the 2,400-sim PUCT target at placements)
cards.hypothesis: The horizon curve: the value seen 5 turns after the opening ranks first picks at Spearman 0.715 / regret 3.6 pts vs 0.633 / 6.4 for the one-ply value the search target reflects and 0.658 / 6.3 for 48 game outcomes. A playout to turn 5 costs ~25 forwards, so 8 spots x 12 playouts (~2,400 forwards) matches the current placement search budget while looking 8 placements + 5 turns deep instead of 2-3 plies. Targets: pi = softmax(V_T / tau) over the plausible spots, z = V_T for the post-pick row (lower variance than the outcome; 'regret through the horizon'). Applies to all 8 placement decisions (reply and second settlements included), which is where the expert gap is largest.
cards.indicator: runs/<run>.agree (62-65 now), runs/<run>.valuetrack (Spearman 0.63), 100-board panel (39.0), Ham (55.4); the actor-side probe first: agreement of the horizon pick itself with the experts (one-ply 65/100, 2,400-sim search 74/100)

Root cause of the 17:14 and 17:21 blow-ups: the actors cache networks by S3 key, a relaunch reuses iteration numbers and keys, so the actors kept serving the diverged first launch's model_0000NN weights for the new learner's iterations (target entropy collapsed to 0.05, policy loss 1e8 within one iteration). Fixed by stopping the actor tasks (cache cleared) and purging shards/models; permanently by a launch token in the control file that makes actors drop their cache (image pushed). Judge at 100k on Spearman and agreement. 20:47 (at ~175k games) DECOUPLED: the playouts now supply only the value label (75% horizon / 25% outcome); the policy target and the move at settlements come from the 2,400-sim search again (engine ee18b4f, image ac0fd129; --placement-horizon-policy restores the coupled form). cards.title: Award reach + port fit block (held)
cards.hypothesis: A watched Gaz game missed an easy block where denying the opponent both awards (4 points of swing at 4 VP) decided the game. The raw facts (road lengths, pieces left, knights played, dev cards, unseen deck) are inputs already, but 'can they still get there' needs road geometry and knight arithmetic the net has to derive; given directly (per seat: roads needed + open extension within that many steps, knights needed + possibly available, reachable flags, points + reachable awards, swing) the main net should price award threats and blocks correctly. Roads were the largest regret category in the self-disagreement probe (28%).

cards.title: Mid-game value label from short-horizon network-only playouts (the opening's decoupling applied to the rest of the game)
cards.hypothesis: The mid-game value target is 75% game outcome + 25% search root value, averaged over siblings; a 15-point game's outcome is a noisy label for a turn-30 position. At placements the turn-5 horizon label beat the outcome (Spearman 0.72 vs 0.66) and, decoupled from the policy, gave the first value-head movement in a million games. An n-step bootstrap mid-game (MuZero/KataGo precedent) should do the same for the value function, which the search curve shows is the floor at ~3.5 pts.
cards.indicator: examples/midgame_horizon.rs + runs/midgame_horizon.py: correlation of each label (z, v1, q400, h3/h5/h10/h20 x 4/12 playouts) with the truth (64-playout win rate) by phase and on open positions (running: 150 games, 8 threads, started 12:53). Then value loss, Spearman, panel, Ham.
cards.launch: BUILT 13:00 Nov 12: SelfPlayConfig midgame_horizon_turns / midgame_playouts (selfplay::midgame_horizon_value: P playouts from each recorded mid-game position to +K turns, mover's value; NaN at placements), SelfPlayData.horizon -> binding 'horizon' -> shards 'horizon' -> az.py --midgame-horizon-turns/--midgame-playouts (actor settings in the control file) and --midgame-horizon-weight wh: value target = (1 - vq - wh) z + vq q + wh h where h exists. Needs an image push + actor cycle (old actors reject the new kwargs). Cost: K-turn playouts x P forwards per recorded position (~15 forwards per 5 turns); measured by the smoke run.
cards.kill: probe: if no horizon label beats the outcome's correlation with the truth on open positions, don't launch
cards.extend: value loss and Spearman move within 100k; panel > on7's
cards.notes: User intent: combine into on7's run once the probe picks K and P (attribution: on7 then carries board heads + mid-game label; note the change point on the board-heads card). | PROBE 13:50 Nov 12 (150 games, 2,141 positions, truth = 64-playout win rate; open positions 0.2-0.8, n=1,008): Pearson with truth: z 0.35, v1 0.74, q400 0.74, h3 0.75/0.77 (4/12 playouts), h5 0.76/0.80, h10 0.74/0.81, h20 0.70/0.81. Playouts matter more than horizon; 5 turns x 12 playouts chosen (~150 forwards/position, ~+35-40% actor cost; smoke: 4 playouts cost +13% at 5 turns). Caveat: truth and labels share the network's bias (bootstrap); the outcome keeps 25%.
